def: To receive property, a trait, or a position from someone before you.
ex: He inherited the house from his aunt.
note: The receiving role contrasts with bequeathing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To slow down, restrict, or prevent a process or action.
ex: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria.
note: Related noun: inhibition, also meaning shyness.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A small container for ink used with a pen.
ex: He dipped his pen into the inkwell.
note: Container and substance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Existing from birth; natural rather than learned.
ex: Some linguists believe language ability is innate.
note: Synonym: inborn. Contrast with acquired.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Introducing a new idea or method.
ex: The team proposed an innovative design.
note: Newness is not itself proof of effectiveness.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: A search for information or an investigation.
ex: The inquiry examined the cause of the failure.
note: Also spelled enquiry in some uses.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To write or carve words on a surface.
ex: Their names were inscribed on the monument.
note: Related noun: inscription.

label: READING
def: Unaware of or unaffected by something.
ex: He seemed insensible to the cold.
note: Not the same as insensitive, meaning unkind.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Unable to be separated; always together.
ex: The two friends were inseparable as children.
note: Contrast with separable.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A deep and clear understanding of something.
ex: The book offers insight into life in ancient Rome.
note: Insightful means showing such understanding.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A careful examination to check condition or quality.
ex: The building failed its safety inspection.
note: Related verb: inspect. An inspector carries out inspections.

label: READING
def: Moving at the same pace as; in agreement with.
ex: Wages have not risen in step with prices.
note: Out of step with means not matching or not in agreement.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To gradually put an idea or feeling into someone's mind.
ex: The teacher instilled confidence in the class.
note: Cause a quality or feeling to develop.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The amount of something taken in, especially food or air.
ex: Doctors recommend reducing your daily intake of salt.
note: Also, the people admitted at one time: this year's intake.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Honesty and strong principles; also, wholeness or soundness.
ex: The repair restored the bridge's structural integrity.
note: Moral and physical senses are both useful.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become or make stronger or more extreme.
ex: The storm intensified as it approached the coast.
note: Related noun: intensity.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop or catch something on its way somewhere.
ex: Guards intercepted the letter before it arrived.
note: In math, an intercept is where a line crosses an axis.

label: READING
def: Able to be exchanged for each other without difference.
ex: The two words are not always interchangeable.
note: Interchangeable parts fit any machine of the same model.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Occurring at intervals, with breaks.
ex: Intermittent rain continued through the day.
note: Contrast with continuous.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Relating to relationships and communication between people.
ex: The job requires strong interpersonal skills.
note: Contrast with intrapersonal, within one person.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To frighten someone, especially to make them obey.
ex: The bully tried to intimidate the younger children.
note: Being intimidated means feeling frightened or overawed.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Understood immediately without conscious step-by-step reasoning.
ex: The answer seemed intuitive but needed checking.
note: An intuition can be wrong.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Without achieving the desired result.
ex: They searched in vain for the missing note.
note: Effort without the intended success.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Always, without exception.
ex: In the story, the signal invariably precedes the visitor.
note: Stronger than usually or frequently.

label: READING
def: To call upon something as a reason, authority, or explanation.
ex: The lawyer invoked an old law to support her case.
note: Can also mean to call upon a god for help.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Done without conscious control or choice.
ex: A sneeze is an involuntary reaction.
note: Contrast with voluntary or deliberate.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Involving a contrast between what is expected or said and what happens or is meant.
ex: It was ironic that the warning sign caused the accident.
note: Not every coincidence is irony.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not connected to the question or issue being considered.
ex: The fact was true but irrelevant to the claim.
note: Truth and relevance are separate tests.

label: READING
def: In a way that can never be recovered or put right.
ex: The files were irretrievably lost in the fire.
note: Close in meaning to irreversibly.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Impossible to undo or change back.
ex: The damage to the forest was irreversible.
note: Contrast with reversible or temporary.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Supplying land with water through channels or pipes.
ex: Irrigation turned the desert into farmland.
note: Remedy : problem pairs, like irrigation : drought.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A member of a jury in a court case.
ex: Each juror listened carefully to the witnesses.
note: Member : group, like juror : jury.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A reason offered to support a claim or action.
ex: The decision lacked a clear justification.
note: A justification can be weak or strong.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A young person or animal; also, childish.
ex: The court handles cases involving juveniles.
note: As an adjective, can criticize immature behavior.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: The folded-back part of the front of a jacket.
ex: He pinned the badge to his lapel.
note: Part of an item of clothing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Present but hidden or not yet developed.
ex: The crisis revealed his latent talent for leadership.
note: Contrast with manifest or evident.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To wash clothing or fabric.
ex: The hotel launders its sheets daily.
note: The ordinary sense is washing; a financial sense also exists.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make laws.
ex: Parliament legislated to protect children from dangerous work.
note: A legislator makes laws; legislate is to law as compose is to music.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Allowed, proper, or reasonably justified.
ex: The criticism raised a legitimate concern.
note: Context may concern legality or good grounds.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A shaped transparent piece that bends light.
ex: A scratch damaged the camera lens.
note: An optical component, not the scratch itself.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A false written statement that damages someone's reputation.
ex: The newspaper was sued for libel.
note: Libel is written; slander is spoken.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Officially permitted to do or own something.
ex: Only a licensed electrician may do this work.
note: Related noun: license, an official permit.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A metal rod that safely directs lightning into the ground.
ex: A lightning rod protected the church tower.
note: Figuratively, a person who attracts criticism.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To walk unevenly because of injury or weakness; also, that manner of walking.
ex: He walked with a slight limp.
note: As an adjective, limp means lacking firmness.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: The scientific study of language.
ex: Linguistics examines how languages work.
note: A field of study, not simply speaking many languages.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A group of young animals born at the same time; also, trash.
ex: The cat gave birth to a litter of five kittens.
note: Group : member, like litter : kitten.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Very tall; also, noble or grand in ideas.
ex: The speech was full of lofty ideals.
note: Can also mean proud and superior.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To want something very strongly.
ex: She longed for news from home.
note: A strong desire, not simply a passing preference.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Believed or kept for a long time.
ex: New evidence challenged a long-held theory.
note: Often paired with belief, view, or assumption.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Applying oil or grease to reduce friction.
ex: The engine failed from a lack of lubrication.
note: Remedy : problem pairs, like lubrication : friction.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Producing a large profit.
ex: The new contract proved lucrative.
note: Financial gain, not simply usefulness.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival.
ex: The winner was magnanimous toward the loser.
note: Magnanimously describes acting with this generosity.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Someone who pretends to be ill to avoid work or duty.
ex: The supervisor wrongly accused her of being a malingerer.
note: Pretended illness, not ordinary illness.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A hard stone often used in sculpture or buildings.
ex: The statue was carved from marble.
note: Here, a material; a marble can also be a small glass ball.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Small in amount or importance; also, at an edge.
ex: The change produced only a marginal improvement.
note: Usually limited, not necessarily zero.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Relating to the sea.
ex: Marine biologists study life in the ocean.
note: A marine is also a soldier serving on ships.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: An upright pole supporting sails or equipment on a ship.
ex: The flag flew from the mast.
note: A mast is part of a ship; a ship can belong to a fleet.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A process or system by which something works or happens.
ex: Scientists studied the mechanism of memory.
note: Also, the moving parts of a machine.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A person who helps opposing sides reach agreement.
ex: A mediator helped settle the dispute.
note: The mediator helps the parties agree.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A person trained to give medical care, often in an emergency.
ex: A medic treated the injured runner.
note: A role defined by care, not by one specific instrument.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To preserve the memory of a person or event.
ex: The monument memorializes the rescue.
note: An action intended to support remembrance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who buys and sells goods, especially in trade.
ex: The merchants brought silk from the East.
note: Related noun: merchandise, the goods for sale.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: A comparison that describes one thing as another.
ex: The writer uses a bridge as a metaphor for communication.
note: Match the intended roles, not every physical detail.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Extremely careful about details.
ex: The historian kept meticulous records.
note: A stronger degree of carefulness.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A very large and important city.
ex: Tokyo is a vast metropolis of millions of people.
note: Related adjective: metropolitan.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To move from one region to another, often seasonally.
ex: The birds migrate south every autumn.
note: Emigrate means leaving a country; migrate is more general.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Extremely small.
ex: A minuscule error ruined the whole experiment.
note: Often misspelled miniscule. A stronger degree of small.

label: READING
def: Based on a mistaken idea or poor judgment.
ex: The plan was misconceived from the beginning.
note: Related noun: misconception.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Improper or unacceptable behavior, especially by a professional.
ex: The officer was dismissed for misconduct.
note: Stronger than a mistake; a breach of rules.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who hoards money and hates spending it.
ex: The miser lived in poverty despite his wealth.
note: A miser is extreme; a frugal person is sensibly careful.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To cause someone to form a wrong belief or take a wrong direction.
ex: The inaccurate map misled the hikers.
note: Can be intentional or unintentional.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To describe something falsely or misleadingly.
ex: The summary misrepresented her argument.
note: A distortion of the original meaning.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Avoiding extremes or excess.
ex: The speaker called for moderation.
note: Moderation reduces extremity, not necessarily all disagreement.

label: READING
def: A change made to something, usually to improve it.
ex: The design needed only minor modification.
note: Related verb: modify.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To make slightly wet.
ex: Moisten the cloth before wiping the table.
note: A weaker degree than soaking.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A system of government in which a king or queen rules.
ex: France was a monarchy before the revolution.
note: Adjective: monarchical. Contrast with republic.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Relating to money.
ex: The winner received a monetary reward.
note: An adjective identifying the kind of value.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A picture made from small pieces of stone, glass, or tile.
ex: The floor was decorated with a Roman mosaic.
note: Figuratively, a mixture of many different parts.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A reason for doing something.
ex: The police could find no motive for the crime.
note: Related noun: motivation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Dark and dirty; also, unclear or suspicious.
ex: The details of the deal remain murky.
note: Contrast with clear or transparent.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A soft, low, continuous sound, especially of voices.
ex: A murmur of approval spread through the crowd.
note: A weaker degree of sound, as a whisper is to a shout.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: In a way that applies to each of two or more sides.
ex: The arrangements were mutually beneficial.
note: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A traditional story explaining beliefs; also, a widely held false belief.
ex: It is a myth that goldfish have short memories.
note: Related noun: mythology.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who plans and directs the route of a ship or plane.
ex: The navigator plotted a course using the stars.
note: Role : task pairs, like navigator : route.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To cancel the effect of something; to deny.
ex: One mistake can negate months of hard work.
note: Related noun: negation.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Too small or unimportant to matter much.
ex: The delay had a negligible effect.
note: Not necessarily exactly zero.

label: READING
def: To reach agreement through discussion; also, to get past an obstacle.
ex: The truck slowly negotiated the narrow mountain road.
note: The travel sense often surprises readers.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The highest social class; also, the quality of being noble.
ex: Members of the nobility owned most of the land.
note: Moral nobility means honesty and generosity.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: An accepted standard or usual pattern.
ex: The result differed from the norm.
note: A norm need not be a moral rule.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: At least one does not; less than everyone or everything.
ex: Not all the lights were on.
note: Does not mean none.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Despite; in spite of.
ex: The project continued, the setbacks notwithstanding.
note: A concession signal, not a cause signal.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To supply what is needed for growth or health.
ex: The food nourished the recovering animal.
note: To provide nourishment, not simply to contain food.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: New and original; as a noun, a long fictional book.
ex: The scientist proposed a novel solution to the problem.
note: Novel (new) differs from novice (beginner).

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A beginner with little experience.
ex: The course is designed for novices.
note: Contrast with expert or veteran.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A person or thing that causes annoyance or inconvenience.
ex: The repeated noise was a nuisance.
note: Not necessarily a serious danger.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A long pole with a flat blade, used to row a boat.
ex: She pulled hard on the oar to reach the shore.
note: The tool used for rowing, as a paddle is for a canoe.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: A reason for disagreeing with a claim or action.
ex: She raised an objection to the proposed method.
note: An objection need not disprove the entire proposal.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Based on facts rather than personal feelings; also, a goal.
ex: The researcher sought an objective measure.
note: As a noun, objective means an aim.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something you must do because of a law, promise, or duty.
ex: Parents have a legal obligation to send their children to school.
note: Related: oblige; obliged means required (or grateful); obligatory means compulsory.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not well known or difficult to understand; also, to hide or make unclear.
ex: The detail was buried in an obscure source.
note: Notice whether the word is an adjective or a verb.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A building with telescopes for watching the stars and planets.
ex: Astronomers at the observatory tracked the comet for weeks.
note: Place and activity: an observatory is where observation happens.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: No longer used because something newer has replaced it.
ex: The device became obsolete.
note: Different from merely old.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Having no smell at all.
ex: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it is odorless and invisible.
note: From odor (a smell); compare tasteless and colorless.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: An illegal act or a crime; also, a feeling of being insulted.
ex: Driving without a license is a serious offense.
note: To take offense means to feel hurt or insulted; in sport, the attacking side.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To perform an official role at an event or ceremony.
ex: She was asked to officiate at the wedding.
note: An official's role differs from an ordinary participant's role.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Out of tune; not matching the correct musical notes.
ex: His off-key singing made the whole audience wince.
note: Also figurative: an off-key remark is unsuitable for the situation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To leave out or fail to include something.
ex: The editor omitted two paragraphs to shorten the article.
note: Noun: omission; an omission can be deliberate or accidental.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: As the representative of, or for the benefit of.
ex: She spoke on behalf of the group.
note: Check whether representation or benefit is intended.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: On the necessary condition that.
ex: A parcel is express only if it has a red label.
note: The condition after only if is required.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Willing to consider new ideas and opinions without prejudice.
ex: An open-minded judge listens carefully to both sides.
note: Contrast with narrow-minded or dogmatic.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Best under the relevant conditions or for a specified aim.
ex: The team searched for the optimal route.
note: Best depends on the criterion being used.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A piece of land where fruit trees are grown.
ex: We picked apples in the orchard behind the farmhouse.
note: Pairs in analogies: orchard is to fruit trees as vineyard is to grapes.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Knowing one's position or direction; also, an introduction to a new setting.
ex: The map helped her regain her orientation.
note: Context determines direction, introduction, or general attitude.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies birds.
ex: The ornithologist recorded the migration routes of the storks.
note: Specialist and subject: ornithologist to birds, as entomologist to insects.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To exclude someone from a group or social contact.
ex: The group ostracized the member who broke its rule.
note: Social exclusion.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: If not, or in other respects.
ex: Leave now; otherwise, you will miss the bus.
note: Read the local sense rather than applying one fixed translation.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: No longer current, modern, or useful.
ex: The factory still relies on outdated machinery from the 1970s.
note: Close to obsolete, which is stronger: no longer used at all.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To describe the main points of something without full detail.
ex: The manager outlined the new plan in a short meeting.
note: As a noun, an outline is a summary or the edge shape of an object.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To defeat or overcome with greater strength or force.
ex: The defenders were overpowered.
note: Overpowering achieves an outcome; trying to overpower may fail.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To remove a ruler or government from power by force.
ex: The rebels tried to overthrow the military regime.
note: Stronger than criticize or oppose: it means actually removing from power.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A sea shellfish with a rough, hinged shell that can produce pearls.
ex: A single oyster may take years to form a pearl.
note: Producer and product: oyster to pearl, as bee to honey.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small group of people chosen to discuss, judge, or advise.
ex: A panel of experts reviewed the research proposals.
note: Also a flat piece of material, as in a solar panel.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An apparent contradiction or a result that seems contrary to expectation.
ex: The result presents a paradox for the theory.
note: An apparent paradox may have an explanation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Loss of the ability to move part or all of the body.
ex: The accident caused temporary paralysis in his left arm.
note: Figuratively, a complete inability to act: political paralysis.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An organism that lives on or in another and feeds on it.
ex: The tick is a parasite that feeds on the blood of animals.
note: Figuratively, a person who lives off others without giving back.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: An umbrella-like object used for shade from the sun.
ex: She opened a parasol on the beach.
note: Protection from sun is the defining purpose.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To forgive or officially release from punishment.
ex: The ruler granted a pardon.
note: A pardon differs from a verdict of not guilty.

label: READING
def: To analyze a sentence by breaking it into its grammatical parts.
ex: The students parsed each sentence to find the subject and verb.
note: More broadly, to examine something closely in order to understand it.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Incomplete; also, biased toward one side.
ex: The report offered only a partial explanation.
note: Check whether incompleteness or bias is meant.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To announce a court's punishment.
ex: The judge passed sentence after the trial.
note: A judge performs this action.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An activity done regularly for enjoyment in one's free time.
ex: Reading detective novels is her favorite pastime.
note: A pastime is chosen for pleasure, unlike a job or duty.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To touch gently with a flat hand.
ex: She patted the dog's head.
note: A mild form of contact, unlike striking hard.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who gives money or support to an artist or cause.
ex: The wealthy patron paid for the young painter's studies.
note: Also a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A very poor person.
ex: The story follows a prince and a pauper.
note: Poverty is part of the word's meaning.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make it easier for something to happen later.
ex: Early experiments paved the way for modern vaccines.
note: Similar to lay the groundwork; the result comes afterward.

label: READING
def: Strange or unusual, often in a slightly disturbing way.
ex: There was a peculiar smell coming from the basement.
note: Peculiar to means belonging only to: a custom peculiar to the region.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The way something is sensed or understood.
ex: Public perception differed from the measured result.
note: A perception need not match reality.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Likely to spoil or decay quickly, especially food.
ex: Milk and fish are perishable, so keep them refrigerated.
note: Opposite: durable or long-lasting; related verb: perish.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Allowed by rules or law.
ex: Using a calculator is not permissible during this test.
note: Close to permitted; opposite: forbidden or prohibited.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To continue to exist or to keep doing something despite difficulty.
ex: If the pain persists, you should see a doctor.
note: Adjective: persistent; noun: persistence.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To cause someone to accept an idea or decide to act.
ex: She persuaded him to reconsider.
note: Unlike merely urging, successful persuasion changes a view or decision.

label: READING
def: A scholar who studies languages and texts, especially their history.
ex: The philologist traced the word back to ancient Greek.
note: Specialist and field: philologist to language, as historian to the past.

label: READING
def: Relating to the sounds of human speech.
ex: The dictionary gives a phonetic spelling to show pronunciation.
note: Noun: phonetics, the study of speech sounds.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A medical doctor.
ex: The physician examined the patient.
note: A physician treats; a vaccine helps prevent disease.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A very small hole.
ex: A pinhole let light into the box.
note: A smaller degree within the category hole.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A jug used to hold and pour liquid.
ex: She poured juice from the pitcher.
note: Here, a container; it can also mean a baseball player.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A deadly disease that spreads quickly; also, anything that causes great trouble.
ex: A plague swept through medieval Europe.
note: As a verb, to plague means to trouble repeatedly.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A long, flat piece of wood.
ex: They used a plank to bridge the ditch.
note: Material shaped into a usable piece.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Reasonable enough to seem possible or believable.
ex: The proposal offered a plausible explanation.
note: Plausible is weaker than proven.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To make an emotional or earnest request; also, to state a legal position.
ex: She pleaded with him to stay.
note: A plea does not guarantee compliance.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To steal goods by force, especially during conflict.
ex: The invaders plundered the town.
note: A specific kind of taking.

label: READING
def: A starting point for a journey, discussion, or line of thought.
ex: The author uses a childhood memory as a point of departure.
note: Also the literal place a journey begins.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A survey of people's opinions, or the process of voting.
ex: A recent poll shows most citizens support the new law.
note: The polls also means the place of voting: a polling station.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To provide a place with inhabitants, or to live in it.
ex: Settlers populated the island.
note: A place can become inhabited.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A person employed to carry luggage or other loads.
ex: The porter carried the suitcases upstairs.
note: The luggage is the object of the work.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A picture or description of a particular person.
ex: The artist painted a portrait of her father.
note: A self-portrait represents the artist herself or himself.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To represent or describe someone or something in a certain way.
ex: The film portrays the scientist as a lonely genius.
note: Noun: portrayal. Related: portrait.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A hole in a road surface.
ex: The driver avoided the deep pothole.
note: A defect in a surface.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who makes pots and dishes from clay.
ex: The potter shaped the wet clay on a spinning wheel.
note: Maker and product: potter to pottery, as weaver to cloth.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Focused on practical results and workable solutions.
ex: She took a pragmatic approach to the problem.
note: Practical emphasis, rather than a guarantee of moral correctness.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To come before in time or order.
ex: A warning preceded the announcement.
note: Contrast with succeed in the sense of come after.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Rain, snow, or hail that falls to the ground.
ex: The region receives very little precipitation in summer.
note: In chemistry, the forming of a solid from a liquid.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: To prevent or make impossible.
ex: The narrow entrance precludes entry by large vehicles.
note: Stronger than merely making an action difficult.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
ex: The lion is the main predator on the savanna.
note: Opposite role: prey; adjective: predatory.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person or thing that came before another in the same role.
ex: The new director changed her predecessor's policy.
note: Contrast with successor.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Decided or fixed in advance.
ex: Each player moves according to a predetermined set of rules.
note: Contrast with spontaneous or chosen on the spot.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: A statement on which an argument is based.
ex: The conclusion follows only if the premise is true.
note: Premise and conclusion have different jobs.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something that must exist or happen before something else can.
ex: A basic course in statistics is a prerequisite for this class.
note: Close to precondition; do not confuse with perquisite (a perk).

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Respect and admiration earned through success or high status.
ex: The university enjoys great prestige around the world.
note: Adjective: prestigious.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To suppose something is true without full proof.
ex: I presume the meeting is canceled, since nobody has arrived.
note: Also to act too boldly; adjective: presumptuous.

label: READING
def: To assume something in advance as a basis for an argument.
ex: The plan presupposes that the budget will not be cut.
note: Noun: presupposition; similar to take for granted.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A false reason given to hide the real reason for an action.
ex: He visited on the pretext of borrowing a book.
note: A pretext is an excuse, not the true motive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Most common or influential at a particular time.
ex: The finding challenged the prevailing view.
note: Common acceptance does not establish truth.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Common or widespread.
ex: The belief was prevalent at the time.
note: Prevalence concerns how common something is.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make a small hole in something with a sharp point.
ex: She pricked her finger on a thorn in the garden.
note: A needle or thorn pricks; the result is a tiny puncture.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Main or most important; also, the head of a school.
ex: The principal reason was cost.
note: Do not confuse with principle.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A basic rule, belief, or standard.
ex: The decision violated their stated principle.
note: Different from principal, meaning main.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Existing or happening before something else.
ex: No prior experience is needed for this job.
note: Prior to means before; noun: priority.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A special right or advantage given only to certain people.
ex: Having a private tutor was a privilege few students enjoyed.
note: Adjective: privileged; contrast with a right shared by everyone.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To investigate or examine closely.
ex: The committee probed the causes of the accident.
note: Also a noun: an investigation or a device for exploring.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Very great or intense; also, showing deep understanding.
ex: The discovery had a profound effect on modern medicine.
note: Opposite: superficial or shallow.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An official rule forbidding something.
ex: The city introduced a prohibition on smoking in parks.
note: Verb: prohibit; opposite: permission.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To increase rapidly in number or spread widely.
ex: Online news sites have proliferated over the past decade.
note: Noun: proliferation; stronger than simply grow.

label: READING
def: Continuing for a long time, often longer than expected.
ex: Prolonged exposure to the sun can damage the skin.
note: Verb: prolong, to make something last longer.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Noticeable, important, or projecting outward.
ex: The tower is a prominent feature of the town.
note: Being prominent may make something easier to locate.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To help something grow or succeed; also, to raise someone's job rank.
ex: Regular exercise and a balanced diet promote good health.
note: Noun: promotion, which can also mean advertising a product.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Biased information spread to influence public opinion.
ex: The regime used radio propaganda to glorify its leader.
note: Propaganda aims to persuade, not to inform fairly.

label: READING
def: To spread ideas or beliefs widely; also, to breed plants.
ex: The group propagated its views through leaflets and speeches.
note: Noun: propagation; related to propaganda.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who supports an idea or proposal.
ex: Proponents argued that the change would help.
note: Contrast with opponent.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A part's size relative to a whole.
ex: A larger proportion of the group agreed.
note: A larger proportion need not mean a larger number.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The legal process of charging someone with a crime; also, the side bringing the case.
ex: The prosecution presented evidence against the accused.
note: Verb: prosecute. The opposing side in a trial is the defense.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Success and material well-being.
ex: The region experienced a period of prosperity.
note: Usually concerns flourishing economic conditions.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Only on the condition that.
ex: You may enter provided that you show a ticket.
note: Introduces a condition.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Supplies of food and other necessities, especially for a journey.
ex: The explorers carried provisions for three months.
note: In the singular, a provision is also a condition in a law or contract.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Something that causes or is intended to cause a reaction, often anger.
ex: He stayed calm despite the provocation.
note: An intended effect is not always an achieved effect.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Nearness in space, time, or relationship.
ex: The station's proximity made the area attractive.
note: Nearness, not necessarily direct contact.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Careful and sensible about possible consequences.
ex: Keeping a reserve was a prudent decision.
note: Contrast with reckless.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A small hole made by something sharp; also, to make such a hole.
ex: A nail caused a puncture in the tire.
note: A defect is different from the material escaping through it.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To claim or appear to do or be something.
ex: The document purports to explain the entire event.
note: The word leaves room to doubt the claim.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To postpone something to a later time.
ex: They put off the meeting until next week.
note: Also to discourage: the smell put me off the food.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To trust or believe in someone or something completely.
ex: Many voters put their faith in the young candidate.
note: Similar to rely on; the trust may later prove mistaken.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Difficult to understand or explain.
ex: The results of the experiment were puzzling to everyone.
note: Similar to baffling or perplexing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Having the skills or training needed for a job or task.
ex: Only a qualified electrician should repair the wiring.
note: A qualified statement is limited or partial, not complete.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To satisfy thirst or put out a fire.
ex: The cool water quenched his thirst.
note: Learn both common senses; neither simply means drink.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Very strong anger; as a verb, to express that anger.
ex: He raged at the unfair decision.
note: A stronger degree of anger.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A protective rail that helps prevent people from falling.
ex: She held the railing on the stairs.
note: Object and protective purpose.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A consequence, often indirect or complicated.
ex: They discussed the policy's possible ramifications.
note: A result that may extend beyond the immediate effect.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Based on reason rather than impulse or unsupported belief.
ex: She offered a rational explanation.
note: Rational does not automatically mean correct.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A field of activity or interest; also, a kingdom.
ex: The question lies outside the realm of science.
note: Within the realm of possibility means possible.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A person or machine that cuts and gathers a crop.
ex: The reaper moved through the wheat field.
note: A role or tool connected to harvesting.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who fights against or refuses to obey authority.
ex: The rebels seized control of the northern province.
note: As a verb (to reBEL), to resist authority; noun: rebellion.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Given or felt by each side toward the other; mutual.
ex: The two countries signed a reciprocal trade agreement.
note: In math, the reciprocal of a number is 1 divided by it.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To restore friendly relations or make apparently conflicting things fit.
ex: The mediator tried to reconcile the neighbors.
note: Resolving a conflict does not mean proving one side correct.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To tell the details of an event.
ex: He recounted the journey.
note: Different from counting something again, which is another sense.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Unnecessary because it repeats or adds nothing needed.
ex: The final sentence was redundant.
note: Redundancy is repetition without useful added work.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A vote by all citizens on a single political question.
ex: The government held a referendum on the new constitution.
note: Unlike an election, which chooses people, a referendum decides an issue.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop yourself from doing something.
ex: Please refrain from talking during the performance.
note: Usually followed by from; as a noun, the repeated chorus of a song.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To show that a claim is false.
ex: One clear counterexample refuted the universal claim.
note: Stronger than denying or disagreeing.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Without being affected by a stated factor.
ex: The fee is fixed regardless of age.
note: The stated factor does not change the result.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A government, especially one that rules strictly or unfairly.
ex: The regime banned all opposition newspapers.
note: Also a system of rules or control: a tax regime.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A large permanent unit of soldiers in an army.
ex: His grandfather served in a cavalry regiment.
note: Part and whole: soldier to regiment, as player to team.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To control something by rules or to keep it at a steady level.
ex: The body regulates its temperature by sweating.
note: Noun: regulation, an official rule.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To strengthen or provide additional support.
ex: The new finding reinforced the earlier conclusion.
note: Strengthening is not always conclusive proof.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Straps used to guide an animal, especially a horse.
ex: She pulled gently on the reins.
note: A tool for control; figuratively, authority.

label: READING
def: To explain or understand something in a new or different way.
ex: The film reinterprets a classic story for modern audiences.
note: Noun: reinterpretation; implies an earlier interpretation existed.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Connected to the matter being considered.
ex: Only one option was relevant to the cause of the change.
note: An interesting fact may still be irrelevant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The extent to which something is dependable or consistent.
ex: They tested the instrument's reliability.
note: Reliable repeated readings can still be systematically inaccurate.

label: READING
def: The raised or hollowed shape of a surface; also, a feeling of ease.
ex: The map shows the mountain's relief in shades of brown.
note: More common meaning: the ease felt when worry or pain ends.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Unwilling or hesitant.
ex: He was reluctant to change his plan.
note: Reluctance does not mean refusal in every case.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small part that remains after the rest is gone.
ex: Only remnants of the ancient wall still stand.
note: Close to residue and remains; the whole no longer exists.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Deep regret for wrongdoing.
ex: She expressed remorse for the harm she caused.
note: Regret specifically connected to wrongdoing.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To formally give up a right, claim, or belief.
ex: He renounced his citizenship and moved abroad.
note: Noun: renunciation; stronger and more formal than stop.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To feel regret for wrongdoing and wish to change.
ex: He repented of his cruelty.
note: More than simply noticing an error.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: An exact copy of an object, often smaller.
ex: The museum displays a replica of the ancient ship.
note: A replica copies an original; it is not a fake meant to deceive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Repeating a study or making a copy.
ex: Replication produced similar results.
note: Repeated support increases confidence without proving every interpretation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The use of force to control people and limit their freedom.
ex: Years of repression led to mass protests.
note: In psychology, pushing painful memories out of awareness.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To express official or strong disapproval.
ex: The worker received a reprimand.
note: To reprimand someone is to rebuke them.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To express disapproval of someone's behavior.
ex: The teacher reproved the pupil for cheating.
note: Close to reprimand.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A doubt or qualification; also, a booking.
ex: She supported the plan with reservations.
note: Here, reservations are limits on her support.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To live in a particular place.
ex: Most members reside nearby.
note: A place of residence is where someone lives.

label: READING
def: What remains after the main part has gone or been removed.
ex: A sticky residue was left where the label had been.
note: Similar to remnant; plural: residues.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Able to recover after difficulty or strain.
ex: The community proved resilient after the flood.
note: Recovery after pressure, rather than never facing pressure.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not easily harmed or affected by something; opposing change.
ex: This fabric is resistant to water and stains.
note: Noun: resistance; heat-resistant, drug-resistant.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Skill in finding ways to solve problems with what is available.
ex: Her resourcefulness helped them repair the boat.
note: Different from merely possessing many resources.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To hold back, control, or limit.
ex: She restrained her anger.
note: Preventing an action is stronger than merely advising against it.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A rule or limit on what people can do.
ex: The city placed restrictions on water use during the drought.
note: Verb: restrict; opposite: freedom or permission.

label: READING
def: To keep or continue to have something.
ex: The old building retains much of its original charm.
note: Noun: retention; opposite: lose or release.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To move back or withdraw, especially from danger.
ex: The army retreated after heavy losses.
note: Also a quiet place for rest.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Looking back at past events.
ex: In retrospect, the warning signs were clear.
note: Hindsight differs from what was known at the time.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Money that a business or government receives, especially from sales.
ex: The company's revenue doubled after the product launch.
note: Revenue is income before costs; profit is what remains after costs.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A return to strength, popularity, or use after a decline.
ex: The 1990s saw a revival of interest in vinyl records.
note: Verb: revive; contrast with decline.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To move in a circle around a central point.
ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun once a year.
note: Figuratively, to revolve around means to center on: the plot revolves around a theft.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A strong feeling of disgust or rejection.
ex: The cruelty filled him with revulsion.
note: Stronger than mild dislike.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Language used to persuade; sometimes, persuasive words lacking substance.
ex: The speech relied on forceful rhetoric.
note: The term can be neutral or critical.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Mockery intended to make someone seem foolish.
ex: The proposal met with ridicule.
note: Contrast with respect, not merely disagreement.

label: READING
def: Strict and unwilling to change; also, stiff and not bendable.
ex: The school had rigid rules about uniforms.
note: Opposite: flexible.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person or group competing with another for the same goal.
ex: The two companies have been rivals for decades.
note: Noun: rivalry, the state of competing.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Strong, sturdy, or able to remain effective under changing conditions.
ex: The conclusion was robust across several analyses.
note: Robust evidence is stronger than a fragile result.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person whose behavior others admire and copy.
ex: The coach is a role model for many young athletes.
note: Being a role model is about example, not formal authority.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To officially introduce a new product, service, or plan.
ex: The company will roll out the new app next month.
note: Noun: rollout; often gradual, region by region.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: One of the horizontal bars that form the steps of a ladder.
ex: He climbed carefully, testing each rung of the ladder.
note: Part and whole: rung to ladder, as step to staircase.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make holy, or to give something official or moral approval.
ex: The ceremony was meant to sanctify the new temple.
note: Related noun: sanctity; compare sanctuary, a holy or safe place.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The liquid that carries food through a plant.
ex: Maple syrup is made from tree sap.
note: As a verb, to gradually weaken: the heat sapped her energy.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Available in only small amounts.
ex: Fresh water was scarce.
note: Contrast with plentiful or abundant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Secretly making clever, dishonest plans to get what one wants.
ex: The scheming adviser plotted to replace the king.
note: From scheme; carries a negative sense, unlike simply planning.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Extremely hot, enough to burn.
ex: The scorching sun dried the fields within days.
note: A stronger degree of hot or warm.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: The written script for a film.
ex: The novel was adapted into a screenplay.
note: A script is different from the finished performance.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To write or draw quickly and carelessly.
ex: He scribbled a note on the envelope.
note: Manner of performing an action.

label: READING
def: Sacred writings of a religion.
ex: The monks spent hours studying ancient scripture.
note: Often plural: the scriptures.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Close and careful examination.
ex: The claim did not survive scrutiny.
note: A careful examination, not a quick glance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who travels by sea, especially a sailor.
ex: Early seafarers navigated by the stars.
note: Related adjective: seafaring.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Experienced through long practice.
ex: A seasoned reporter knows which questions to ask.
note: Of food, it means flavored with salt or spices.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A very young plant grown from a seed.
ex: The seedling produced its first leaves.
note: An early stage in development.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Clear without needing further explanation or proof.
ex: He treated the rule as self-evident.
note: What someone treats as obvious may still be questioned.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Calmness and peacefulness.
ex: The garden gave her a sense of serenity.
note: Contrast with agitation.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To cut off or break a connection completely.
ex: The decision severed their business ties.
note: A stronger separation than loosening.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To break suddenly into many small pieces.
ex: The glass shattered when it hit the floor.
note: Figuratively, hopes or confidence can also be shattered.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To lose or get rid of something naturally.
ex: Many trees shed their leaves in autumn.
note: Also in "shed light on": to help explain.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To postpone or set aside a plan.
ex: The company shelved the project due to lack of funds.
note: Postponed, not necessarily cancelled forever.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A utensil with a mesh for separating fine particles from coarse ones.
ex: She poured the flour through a sieve.
note: A tool and its action: a sieve is used to sift.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To pass material through a sieve to separate parts.
ex: She sifted the flour before baking.
note: The material may remain after impurities are removed.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A sign showing direction; as a verb, to indicate a route or structure.
ex: The signposts helped walkers find the path.
note: Aids orientation.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Treating something complex as if it were much simpler than it is.
ex: His simplistic explanation ignored several key factors.
note: Negative; contrast with simple, which can be positive.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Doubt or a questioning attitude toward a claim.
ex: The surprising result met with skepticism.
note: Skepticism is not automatic rejection.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To read quickly to get the main idea.
ex: She skimmed the article before the meeting.
note: Also, to remove something from a liquid's surface.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A person who hates spending money; a miser.
ex: The old skinflint refused to pay for repairs.
note: Stronger and more negative than frugal.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A small device that launches a stone using stretched elastic.
ex: The boy aimed a slingshot at a target.
note: A projectile-launching device.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Unimportant or operating on a minor scale.
ex: He was only a small-time thief, not a gang leader.
note: Contrast with big-time.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To extract metal from ore by heating and melting it.
ex: Ancient workers smelted copper in simple furnaces.
note: Not to be confused with smelt, a past form of smell.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make or become solid, firm, or fixed.
ex: The lava solidified as it cooled.
note: Figuratively, to strengthen: to solidify an alliance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Alone, single, or preferring to be alone.
ex: A solitary tree stood on the hill.
note: Not necessarily lonely or unhappy.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Able to be dissolved in a liquid.
ex: Salt is soluble in water, but sand is not.
note: A problem can also be soluble, meaning solvable; opposite: insoluble.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A musical composition for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.
ex: The pianist performed a sonata by Mozart.
note: A type of musical work, as a sonnet is a type of poem.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To plant seeds by scattering or placing them in the ground.
ex: Farmers sow the fields in spring.
note: Sowing precedes harvesting but does not guarantee a harvest.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A digging tool with a broad blade.
ex: She used a spade to turn the soil.
note: A tool and the work it performs.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A weapon with a long shaft and pointed end.
ex: The guard carried a spear.
note: One member of the category weapon.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The general mood and ideas typical of a particular period.
ex: Her novels captured the spirit of the times.
note: Also known by the German word zeitgeist.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Arising naturally or without deliberate planning.
ex: The audience gave a spontaneous cheer.
note: Unplanned does not mean causeless.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To make popping, spitting sounds, or to speak in a confused, hurried way.
ex: The old engine sputtered and then stopped.
note: Splutter is a close variant.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To waste money, time, or opportunities foolishly.
ex: He squandered his savings on useless gadgets.
note: Contrast with conserve or save.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To speak with pauses and repeated sounds, often from nervousness.
ex: He stammered an apology to the angry customer.
note: Close in meaning to stutter.

label: READING
def: The process of making things conform to one common standard.
ex: Standardization of parts made repairs much easier.
note: Verb: standardize.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem.
ex: The poem has four stanzas of six lines each.
note: Stanza is to poem as paragraph is to essay.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Not moving.
ex: The vehicle remained stationary.
note: Do not confuse with stationery: writing materials.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A strong, unpleasant smell.
ex: A stench came from the blocked drain.
note: The unpleasant quality is part of the meaning.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To remove or destroy microorganisms; also, to prevent reproduction.
ex: The instruments were sterilized before use.
note: Use the sense required by the pair or passage.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To encourage activity, growth, or interest.
ex: The new policy aims to stimulate the economy.
note: Related nouns: stimulus, stimulation.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To pour a liquid through a sieve or cloth to separate out solids.
ex: Strain the pasta before adding the sauce.
note: Also, to stretch or overwork: to strain a muscle.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make great efforts to achieve something.
ex: The team strives for excellence in every game.
note: Past forms: strove, striven.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To play strings by sweeping the fingers across them.
ex: He strummed the guitar softly.
note: An action performed on a particular instrument part.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To speak with involuntary repetition of sounds, especially first sounds.
ex: She stuttered when asked to speak in public.
note: Often a lasting speech condition; compare stammer.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A vessel designed to travel underwater.
ex: The submarine remained below the surface.
note: A special type of vessel.

label: READING
def: To put or keep under water.
ex: The flood submerged the entire village.
note: Opposite: emerge or surface.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Lower in rank or importance; also, to make less important.
ex: The detail is subordinate to the main argument.
note: A subordinate role is secondary.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Coming later.
ex: Subsequent studies challenged the finding.
note: Contrast with prior or preceding.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become less strong or intense; to die down.
ex: The storm finally subsided after midnight.
note: Also, of land, to sink to a lower level.

label: READING
def: To stay alive by means of a particular food or income.
ex: The villagers subsisted on rice and fish.
note: Related noun: subsistence, having just enough to survive.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Large or important in amount or degree.
ex: The revision made a substantial difference.
note: Stronger than slight or marginal.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: So slight or delicate that it is hard to notice or describe.
ex: There is a subtle difference between the two words.
note: The b is silent; noun: subtlety.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Enough for a particular purpose or result.
ex: One valid example is sufficient to show possibility.
note: Sufficient differs from necessary.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The highest point of a mountain.
ex: The climbers reached the summit at dawn.
note: Also, a meeting between heads of government.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Concerning only the surface or lacking depth.
ex: The review offered only a superficial comparison.
note: Surface similarity can hide different relationships.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To stop something by force or to hold back a feeling.
ex: She suppressed a laugh during the lecture.
note: Related noun: suppression.

label: READING
def: To overcome a difficulty or obstacle.
ex: They surmounted many problems to finish on time.
note: Related adjective: insurmountable, impossible to overcome.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: An amount beyond what is needed or used.
ex: The farm sold its surplus grain.
note: Contrast with deficit or shortage.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Easily affected or influenced by something.
ex: The material is susceptible to damage.
note: A vulnerability, not a certainty of damage.

label: READING
def: To support or keep something going over time.
ex: The river sustains the farms along its banks.
note: Related adjective: sustainable.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To set aside pride in order to do something difficult or humbling.
ex: She swallowed her pride and asked for help.
note: An idiom: do not interpret swallow literally.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A unit of pronunciation containing one vowel sound.
ex: The word table has two syllables.
note: A sound unit is different from a letter or a whole word.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A large musical work, usually for an orchestra.
ex: The orchestra performed the symphony.
note: A kind of musical composition.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: An instrument used to draw in or inject liquid.
ex: The nurse prepared a syringe.
note: A tool and its function.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Understood or accepted without being stated.
ex: They had a tacit agreement to avoid the subject.
note: A kind of implicit understanding.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To publicly adopt a position on an issue.
ex: The mayor took a firm stance against the plan.
note: Stance is a position or attitude.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To seek protection or shelter.
ex: The travelers took refuge from the storm.
note: A response to danger or discomfort.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To become established and begin to grow or develop.
ex: The new ideas slowly took root in society.
note: Literally said of plants; figuratively of ideas and habits.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Real and able to be touched or clearly seen.
ex: The program produced tangible results within a year.
note: Opposite: intangible.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Holding firmly or persisting despite difficulty.
ex: The tenacious investigator kept searching.
note: Persistence can describe a person or a grip.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A usual direction or likelihood of behavior.
ex: The group showed a tendency to choose familiar options.
note: A tendency permits exceptions.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Not final or certain; open to change.
ex: The researcher offered a tentative explanation.
note: Contrast with definite or conclusive.

label: READING
def: To bring something to an end.
ex: The company terminated the contract early.
note: Related noun: termination.

label: READING
def: The set of special terms used in a particular field.
ex: Doctors should avoid technical terminology when speaking to patients.
note: Not to be confused with termination.

label: READING
def: Having a healing or calming effect.
ex: Gardening can be therapeutic for stressed people.
note: Related noun: therapy.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: By that means or as a result of that action.
ex: She clarified the rule, thereby reducing confusion.
note: Links an action to its effect.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A small cap worn on the finger to protect it when sewing.
ex: She pushed the needle through with a thimble.
note: A protective tool, like a helmet for the head.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Completely and with careful attention to detail.
ex: He checked the evidence thoroughly.
note: Thoroughness does not automatically imply expertise.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A point or level at which something begins or changes.
ex: The noise crossed the threshold of discomfort.
note: Can be literal, numerical, or figurative.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A story or film designed to create suspense and excitement.
ex: The thriller kept us guessing.
note: A type of story, rather than a production tool.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: Wood prepared for use in building.
ex: The cabin was built from local timber.
note: Tree is to timber as raw material is to processed material.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Slightly drunk.
ex: One drink made him tipsy.
note: A mild degree, rather than extreme drunkenness.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To work very hard for a long time.
ex: The workers toiled in the fields all day.
note: Also a noun meaning exhausting work.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Willingness to accept views or behavior different from one's own.
ex: The school promotes tolerance among students.
note: Also, the ability to endure something, e.g. heat tolerance.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To make something less intense, extreme, or forceful.
ex: The editor asked him to tone down his criticism.
note: Contrast with intensify.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Without success; with no useful result.
ex: They searched for the key, but to no avail.
note: Avail means use or benefit.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To fall over, or to cause to fall; to overthrow.
ex: The strong wind toppled several old trees in the park.
note: Often used for removing leaders from power.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A distinguishing quality or characteristic.
ex: Patience is one of her strongest traits.
note: A trait can be part of a personality.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Calmness and peacefulness.
ex: The early morning brought tranquility.
note: Also spelled tranquillity.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Lasting only a short time.
ex: The effect was transient.
note: Contrast with permanent or enduring.

label: READING
def: To become known, or to turn out.
ex: It transpired that the letter was a forgery.
note: Also used loosely to mean happen.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A slight shaking movement, especially of the ground.
ex: A small tremor was felt before the earthquake.
note: A weaker degree of an earthquake.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A stream or river that flows into a larger river.
ex: The tributary joins the main river upstream.
note: A relation within a river system, not just any river.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To flow slowly in a thin stream.
ex: Water trickled down the cave wall.
note: Weaker than flow; contrast with gush.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A three-legged stand supporting a camera or other equipment.
ex: The camera rested on a tripod.
note: A support tool, not the object being photographed.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Of little value or importance.
ex: They argued over a trivial detail.
note: Related noun: trivia.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Deserving to be trusted.
ex: We need a trustworthy source.
note: Trustworthy describes grounds for trust, not actual trust by everyone.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Using power in a cruel and unfair way.
ex: The tyrannical ruler jailed all his critics.
note: Related nouns: tyrant, tyranny.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Done without official permission.
ex: Unauthorized entry to the lab is forbidden.
note: British spelling: unauthorised.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Not limited or held back.
ex: The discussion was unconstrained by a fixed agenda.
note: Related action: to restrain.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To weaken the basis, confidence, or effectiveness of something.
ex: The new evidence undermined the explanation.
note: Weakening need not prove the opposite.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Clear and allowing only one interpretation.
ex: Her answer was an unequivocal no.
note: Opposite: equivocal or ambiguous; adverb: unequivocally.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: The state of being joined or acting as one.
ex: The disagreement threatened the group's unity.
note: Contrast with division or a split.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To suddenly release a strong force or feeling.
ex: The decision unleashed a wave of protests.
note: Literally, to free a dog from its leash.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Except if.
ex: The gate stays shut unless a guard opens it.
note: Do not casually turn an exception into a two-way rule.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Not known to have happened before.
ex: The city faced an unprecedented demand for water.
note: Different from merely unusual.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To undo twisted or knitted threads; also, to solve a puzzle.
ex: The investigator unraveled the mystery.
note: Literal undoing and figurative clarification.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: To free from twists or knots; to make clear.
ex: It took an hour to untangle the fishing line.
note: Close in meaning to disentangle; opposite: tangle.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To support or confirm a law, decision, or principle.
ex: The court upheld the original ruling.
note: Contrast with overturn.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: To pull out by the roots; also, to displace someone.
ex: The storm uprooted the tree.
note: Literal removal and a related figurative sense.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Needing immediate attention.
ex: They sent an urgent request for help.
note: Urgency can cause haste.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A preparation that helps the body develop protection against a disease.
ex: The vaccine reduced the risk of infection.
note: Prevention is different from treatment.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A person who wanders from place to place without a home.
ex: The vagabond slept in a different town each night.
note: Similar to wanderer or drifter.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Well-founded or acceptable; in logic, having a conclusion that follows.
ex: The objection was valid.
note: A valid logical form can still begin with false premises.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: Excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements.
ex: His vanity made criticism hard to accept.
note: Not the same as sensible self-confidence.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Something that can change or take different values.
ex: Practice time was a variable in the study.
note: Distinguish the changed variable from the measured outcome.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: The supply of fresh air to a room or building.
ex: Poor ventilation made the room stuffy.
note: Verb: ventilate.

label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: The decision reached at the end of a trial.
ex: The jury delivered its verdict after two days.
note: The final result of a trial, as a score is of a game.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: With the order or relationship reversed.
ex: She helps him, and vice versa.
note: The reversed direction must also be stated or justified.

label: READING
def: Careful watchfulness for danger or difficulty.
ex: Constant vigilance helped the guards prevent theft.
note: Adjective: vigilant.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: To show that someone or something was right or wrongly blamed.
ex: The later evidence vindicated her decision.
note: Different from merely defending someone.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Absolutely necessary or essential.
ex: Water is vital for all living things.
note: Also, full of energy; noun: vitality.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Likely to change suddenly; also, easily evaporating.
ex: Prices remained volatile.
note: The financial, emotional, and physical senses differ.

label: READING
def: An amount of money risked on the result of an event; a bet.
ex: He placed a small wager on the race.
note: Also a verb: to wager means to bet.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A collection of someone's clothes; also, a cupboard for clothes.
ex: Her wardrobe contains several formal jackets.
note: Choose collection or container according to context.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: A soft substance, as in candles, that melts when heated.
ex: The candle wax dripped onto the table.
note: As a verb, to grow, as in the moon waxing and waning.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A piece thick at one end and tapering to a thin edge.
ex: She cut a wedge of cheese.
note: A shape or portion, rather than a different substance.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: A small hand-pushed cart, usually with one wheel.
ex: She moved the soil in a wheelbarrow.
note: A manually moved carrier.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: While, when used to contrast two facts.
ex: One group improved, whereas the other did not.
note: A contrast signal.

label: EXAM ANALOGY
def: The act of taking back, removing, or moving away.
ex: The army announced its withdrawal.
note: Context may concern money, forces, participation, or a claim.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: Worth the time, money, or effort spent.
ex: Volunteering at the shelter proved a worthwhile experience for her.
note: Contrast with pointless.

label: EXAM VOCABULARY
def: To produce a result or crop; also, to give way.
ex: The careful experiment yielded some very surprising results.
note: Also, to surrender: to yield to pressure.

label: ADDITIONAL WORD
def: Great energy and enthusiasm for a cause or task.
ex: He approached the campaign with zeal.
note: Strong commitment, not necessarily sound judgment. label: ANALOGY PRACTICE
def: A scientist who studies animals.
ex: The zoologist observed the gorillas for months.
note: Field: zoology, as a botanist studies plants.
